claims.text: W31Ta34Cr5V27Hf3 and HfNbTaTiZr are examples of multiphase refractory high-entropy alloys relevant to the hypothesis.
The Cr-Hf pair in W31Ta34Cr5V27Hf3 has a strongly negative SRO parameter at low temperature.
Hf-Ti pairs in HfNbTaTiZr exhibit attractive chemical ordering and can form B2-type clusters.
Negative SRO parameters indicate a thermodynamic tendency toward chemical ordering.
A solutionized W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf or HfNbTaTiZr alloy can retain significant negative SRO while lacking long-range periodicity.
The predicted ODTT of W31Ta34Cr5V27Hf3 is approximately 1120 K.
In modeled W31Ta34Cr5V27Hf3, a Cr-Hf precipitate is visible at 300 K and vanishes by 620 K.
SRO parameters tend toward zero as W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf approaches its order-disorder transition, indicating homogenization.
The relevant SRO clusters remain stable through intermediate aging temperatures and dissolve only near the ODTT.
Low-temperature negative SRO produces nanoscale ordered clusters or precipitates that impede dislocation motion.
The ordered clusters increase strength while reducing ductility and creating a brittle regime.
Increasing temperature toward the ODTT overcomes the ordering enthalpy and dissolves SRO clusters.
Cluster dissolution restores random-solid-solution character and increases dislocation mobility.
Multiphase RHEAs with strong ordering tendencies will undergo a ductile-brittle-ductile transition as aging temperature increases.
The as-solutionized state has high room-temperature ductility.
Room-temperature elongation reaches a minimum at intermediate aging temperatures where SRO clusters are most stable.
Room-temperature ductility recovers at aging temperatures near the ODTT when SRO vanishes and clusters dissolve.
The transition is restricted to alloys with strong negative SRO and an ODTT below melting or catastrophic phase-separation temperatures.
The transition does not apply to alloys with positive or negligible SRO.

The hypothesis is falsified if ductility remains monotonic, if the ductility minimum does not coincide with maximal SRO or cluster stability, or if ductility fails to recover after SRO and clusters disappear.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as already having significant negative SRO and high ductility, while the mechanism broadly states that strong negative SRO generates ordered clusters and reduced ductility. The hypothesis does not clearly distinguish harmless pairwise SRO in the initial state from the cluster population claimed to cause brittleness.
